title: Superpowers: a feature development workflow
question: How does Superpowers guide a feature from design to branch completion?
summary: A prescribed workflow with execution choices, per-task review, bounded fix loops and final integration decisions.

nodes.label: Choose relevant skills
nodes.description: The entry instructions select skills for the task. This graph follows the feature-design route; debugging and other workflows have other entry points.

nodes.label: Explore & document the design
nodes.description: Clarify intent, goals, constraints and approaches, then write the design. The instructions allow small changes or explicitly agreed exceptions to take a shorter route.

nodes.label: Design approval
nodes.description: The normal feature route requires user-approved design before building, then hands off to writing-plans. This is an instruction gate, not a technical enforcement mechanism.

nodes.label: Write & review the plan
nodes.description: Create a plan with task-sized checkboxes and verification steps. Self-review checks specification coverage, consistency and testing before execution.

nodes.label: Choose execution method
nodes.description: Keep a previously selected method; otherwise the user chooses subagent-driven development or native inline execution. Both are described as same-session workflows.

nodes.label: Subagent-driven controller
nodes.description: Prepare the workspace and ledger, dispatch a fresh implementer per task, answer questions, coordinate task reviews and select subsequent tasks.

nodes.label: Implement, test & self-review
nodes.description: The implementer works on the task, tests, commits and self-reviews. Questions return to the controller for context before work continues.

nodes.label: Per-task review
nodes.description: Review the completed task for specification compliance and code quality. Approval completes the task; findings enter a bounded fix loop.

nodes.label: Bounded fix loop
nodes.description: Up to five fix rounds: resume the original implementer in rounds 1–3 and use fresh, more capable help in rounds 4–5. Re-review the affected scope; at the cap adjudicate, defer or park according to the rules.

nodes.label: Native inline execution
nodes.description: The current agent executes plan steps, uses TDD and verification, handles mismatches, and checks the completion contract before recording each task.

nodes.label: Task ledger & next task
nodes.description: Track plan identity, progress, tests and commits. Finish or park the task under the applicable rules, then continue remaining tasks or move to whole-branch review.

nodes.label: Whole-branch review
nodes.description: Review the complete branch, including deferred and parked issues. Allow one fix wave and one scoped re-review, adjudicate remaining issues and clean the plan workspace when review is clean.

nodes.label: Tests & integration choice
nodes.description: Run the full test suite; failures stop the integration menu. When green, offer the environment-appropriate choices such as merge, push/PR or keeping the branch. The user decides.

sources.excerpt:
## The Rule

**Invoke relevant or requested skills BEFORE any response or action** — including clarifying questions, exploring the codebase, or checking files. If it turns out wrong for the situation, you don't have to use it.

**Before entering plan mode:** if you haven't already brainstormed, invoke the brainstorming skill first.

Then announce "Using [skill] to [purpose]" and follow the skill exactly. If it has a checklist, create a todo per item.

## Skill Priority

When multiple skills apply, process skills come first — they set the approach, then implementation skills (frontend-design, etc.) carry it out. Brainstorming and systematic-debugging are Superpowers' most common process skills, but the rule holds for any of them.

- "Let's build X" → superpowers:brainstorming first, then implementation skills.
- "Fix this bug" → superpowers:systematic-debugging first, then domain skills.

## Red Flags

These thoughts mean STOP—you're rationalizing:

| Thought | Reality |
|---------|---------|

## The Written Design

Write a plain document a talented builder in the domain could plan
from without going back to your human partner. Cover:

- intent and the why
- goals, non-goals, anti-goals
- constraints
- approaches (above)
- the parts of the how they decided, as they decided them
- what's left to the builder

For a small change, the short design covers the same points in a line
or two each and goes straight to your human partner, without the
builder check.

**Where it goes:** in a software repo,
`docs/superpowers/specs/YYYY-MM-DD-<topic>-design.md`, committed.
Otherwise, pick a sensible place and say where. Your human partner's
preferences override both.

**Builder check** (for a project): dispatch a fresh subagent with
`builder-check-prompt.md` in this directory. When you tell your human
partner you're writing it up, say a reviewer will read it first and you
may come back once with a few questions. Don't hand over the document
until the check is back. Sort what the builder asks into three piles:

- **Answered already** by the conversation or the project: put the answer
  in the document.
- **Minor:** a sensible builder could settle it without changing what gets
  built. Settle it yourself and mark it in the document as your call.
- **Theirs:** only your human partner can answer it, and the answer changes
  what gets built.

Bring the "theirs" pile in one message, most important first. Update the
document with their answers, then hand it over with a short list of the
calls you made so they can check those while reading. That's the only
round of questions the check produces. Without a subagent tool, read the
document as that builder yourself.

<HARD-GATE>
Nothing gets built until your human partner approves the design doc:
the short one for a small change, the full one for a project.
Building includes writing product code, scaffolding, installing
dependencies, creating projects, and invoking an implementation skill.
Reading and exploring are fine.

Two exceptions. If they opted out of the questions, the skill is done
and the gate goes with it. A spike they said yes to may be built; it
stays labeled throwaway, and keeping what it produced is a new request
that comes back through this gate.

After the design doc is approved, the next step is the plan: invoke
superpowers:writing-plans and no other skill.

## Plan Document Header

**Every plan MUST start with this header:**

```markdown
# [Feature Name] Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** [One sentence describing what this builds]

**Architecture:** [2-3 sentences about approach]

**Tech Stack:** [Key technologies/libraries]

**Spec:** [path to the spec/design doc this plan implements — the plan
argues from the spec, so the spec travels with it; executors read both]

## Self-Review

After writing the complete plan, look at the spec with fresh eyes and check the plan against it. This is a checklist you run yourself — not a subagent dispatch.

**1. Spec coverage:** Skim each section/requirement in the spec. Can you point to a task that implements it? List any gaps.

**2. Step scan:** Every step must let the implementer write exactly one reasonable thing, and no step may carry more than that: a line that decides nothing is a gap, a function body the signature and tests already determine is a transcript. Fix both.

**3. Type consistency:** Do the types, method signatures, and property names you used in later tasks match what you defined in earlier tasks? A function called `clearLayers()` in Task 3 but `clearFullLayers()` in Task 7 is a bug.

**4. Review Focus:** For each input class or failure mode the spec implies, is there a task whose tests exercise it? The five uncovered ones most likely to bite a person go in the Review Focus section, and each line there gets its test added to the owning task. An empty section means you checked and found none, not that you skipped the check.

**5. Proportion:** Compare the plan's length to the spec's. A plan several times longer than the spec it implements is a transcript of the program, not a plan. If code blocks are most of the document, replace bodies with signatures, test names and assertions, and check that each step is still unambiguous.

If you find issues, fix them inline. No need to re-review — just fix and move on. If you find a spec requirement with no task, add the task.

## Execution Handoff

After saving and self-reviewing the plan, link it for your human partner
to read. If they have already explicitly supplied an execution method, ask
them to review the plan and confirm it captures what they want; wait for that
review before implementation, then use the preserved method. Otherwise, ask
them to review the plan and choose an execution method before implementation.

**When no execution method has already been supplied:**

**"Plan complete and saved to `docs/superpowers/plans/<filename>.md`. Please review the plan. Which execution approach would you prefer?**

- **Subagent-driven** - A fresh subagent implements each task and a fresh reviewer checks it before the next one starts, then a whole-branch review at the end. Most thorough; costs a fresh context per task and per review.
- **Native** - I implement every task myself in this session, the way this harness runs work, then one fresh reviewer on the most capable model checks the whole branch. Cheapest and fastest; no independent review until the end. Runs well with a mid-tier session model, since the plan carries the design.

**For this plan I recommend <one of the two>, because <one sentence from the plan: how much the tasks depend on each other's interfaces, how many there are, what a shipped mistake would cost>. Does the plan capture what you want, and which approach should we use?"**

**When an execution method has already been supplied:**

**"Plan complete and saved to `docs/superpowers/plans/<filename>.md`. Please review the plan. Does it capture what you want?"**

**If Subagent-driven chosen:**
- **REQUIRED SUB-SKILL:** Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development

**If Native chosen:**
- **REQUIRED SUB-SKILL:** Use superpowers:executing-plans

Ensure the work happens in an isolated workspace: use
superpowers:using-git-worktrees to create one or verify the existing one.
Never start implementation on a main/master branch without your human
partner's explicit consent.

Conversation memory does not survive compaction. In real sessions,
controllers that lost their place have re-dispatched entire completed task
sequences — the single most expensive failure observed. Track progress in
a ledger file, not only in todos.

- Each plan owns a workspace: at skill start, run this skill's
  `bash scripts/sdd-workspace PLAN_FILE` by its absolute path, from the
  working tree you're executing in — it prints the plan's git-ignored
  directory (under `<repo-root>/.superpowers/sdd/`), home to
  every artifact for THIS plan: ledger, briefs, reports, review packages.
  Another plan's directory is never yours to read or write.
- Check for this plan's ledger at `<workspace>/progress.md`. If one exists,
  read [references/resuming.md](references/resuming.md) before anything
  else: it says whose ledger it is and where to resume.
- Create the ledger with its identity as the first line:
  `# SDD ledger — plan: <plan file path>`.
- The ledger is your recovery map: the commits it names exist in git even
  when your context no longer remembers creating them. After compaction,
  trust the ledger and `git log` over your own recollection.
- `git clean -fdx` will destroy the workspace (it's git-ignored scratch); if
  that happens, recover from `git log`.

Read the plan once, note its context and Global Constraints, and create a
todo per task. If the plan names a Spec, read that too: the spec is the
authority the plan argues from, and conflicts inside the plan resolve
against it. A plan with no reachable spec gets a ledger note saying so —
rulings made without one are provisional.

Before dispatching Task 1, read [references/preflight.md](references/preflight.md)
and run the conflict scan it describes. Its table and rulings go in the
ledger.

Before the loop starts, two routes leave it immediately:

- Record Minor findings in the progress ledger as you go
  (`Task <N>: minor (deferred): <one-liner>`), and point the final
  whole-branch review at that list so it can triage which must be fixed
  before merge. A roll-up nobody reads is a silent discard. Minor findings
  never enter the loop.
- A finding labeled plan-mandated — or any finding that conflicts with
  what the plan's text requires — is yours to rule on: weigh the finding
  against the plan text, decide with the spec as the binding authority, and
  ledger the ruling before you act on it. Do not dismiss the finding because
  the plan mandates it, and do not dispatch a fix that contradicts the plan
  without a recorded ruling.
Everything else enters the loop. A fix round is one fix dispatch plus one
scoped re-review. Five rounds maximum per task:

**Rounds 1-3 — resume the original implementer.** Send it the open findings
verbatim. Its context is intact: it knows the task, the code, and its own
choices. If your harness cannot send another message to a live subagent,
dispatch a fresh implementer carrying the brief path, the report-file path,
and the findings — the report file is the persistent memory either way.

**Rounds 4-5 — dispatch a fresh implementer on a more capable model** (per
SKILL.md's Model Selection), with the brief path, the report-file path, the open
findings, and this framing: "A prior implementer attempted this task
[N] times; you own it now. Read the report file for what was tried." A loop
that survives three resumes usually means the implementer cannot see its
own problem — fresh eyes and a capability bump in one move.

**Every round, either way:** the implementer fixes, re-runs the tests
covering the amended code, appends its fix report to the same report file,
and returns the short contract. Before re-dispatching the reviewer, confirm
the fix report contains the covering tests, the command run, and the
output; dispatch the re-review once all three are present. Name the
covering test files in the fix message — a one-line fix does not need the
whole suite.

**The re-review is scoped.** Run `bash scripts/review-package PLAN_FILE FIX_BASE HEAD`
by its absolute path, from the working tree you're executing in, where FIX_BASE is the head the previous review saw, and dispatch
[re-review-prompt.md](../re-review-prompt.md) with the findings list, the
brief, the report file, and the printed diff path. The re-reviewer verdicts
each finding ADDRESSED or NOT ADDRESSED and flags new breakage in the fix
diff only. New Critical/Important breakage in the fix diff joins the open
findings list. Out-of-scope observations go to the ledger as deferred
minors — they never extend the loop.

**After each round,** append to the ledger:
`Task <N>: fix round <R>/5 (<X> addressed, <Y> open — <finding one-liners>; commits <a7>..<b7>)`

Never fix findings yourself in the controller session — your context stays
clean for coordination, and controller fixes skip review.

**The breaker.** When round 5's re-review still leaves findings open, stop
dispatching. Adjudicate each open finding yourself — you hold the plan and
the cross-task context the reviewer lacks:

- **The reviewer is wrong, or the point is contestable:** park it —
  `Task <N>: parked — <finding> — Ruling: <why the code stands>`. The final
  review sees both sides.
- **Real, but nothing downstream builds on it:** park it the same way, with
  a ruling that says it's real and deferred.
- **Real and load-bearing** — a later task builds on it, or it reveals a
  plan defect: rule on the smallest change that unblocks the dependent work,
  ledger it as `Task <N>: Ruling: <finding> — <what you decided and why>`,
  and carry it into the next task's dispatch. Parking a structural failure
  silently lets every dependent task build on it. Stop only when the defect
  leaves every path forward a guess.

The final whole-branch review gets a package too: run
`bash scripts/review-package PLAN_FILE MERGE_BASE HEAD` by its absolute path,
from the working tree you're executing in (MERGE_BASE = the commit the
branch started from, e.g. `git merge-base main HEAD`) and include the
printed path in the final review dispatch, so the final reviewer reads
one file instead of re-deriving the branch diff with git commands. Dispatch
on the most capable available model (see SKILL.md's Model Selection), using
superpowers:requesting-code-review's
[code-reviewer.md](../../requesting-code-review/code-reviewer.md). Point it at
the ledger's deferred-minor and parked lines so it can triage which must be
fixed before merge.

If the final whole-branch review returns findings, dispatch ONE fix subagent
with the complete findings list — not one fixer per finding.
Per-finding fixers each rebuild context and re-run suites; a real
session's final-review fix wave cost more than all its tasks combined.
Then run exactly one scoped re-review of the fix wave
(`bash scripts/review-package PLAN_FILE FIX_BASE HEAD` by its absolute path,
from the working tree you're executing in, over the fix range,
[re-review-prompt.md](../re-review-prompt.md)).
Adjudicate any residual findings as in the fix loop's breaker
(references/fix-loop.md): park with rulings, or rule on the load-bearing
ones and ledger what you decided. Only the four things that stop a running
plan (top of SKILL.md) stop you here. There is no second fix wave —
residual load-bearing findings surface to your human partner when
finishing-a-development-branch presents the options.

### Finish

Before you delete anything, collect every ledger line containing `Ruling:` —
preflight rulings, parked findings, breaker adjudications, all of them — into
your final message under "Rulings I made", in the order you made them, each
with what it costs if wrong. The list is exhaustive: if the ledger holds a
ruling, the list holds it. That list is the only place the decisions you
took on your human partner's behalf reach them — they read it and rework
whatever you got wrong. A ruling that dies with the workspace was a decision
made in secret.

When the final whole-branch review is clean and its fixes are merged,
delete this plan's workspace (`rm -rf <workspace>`) — the git history is
the record now. Sibling directories belong to other plans; leave them
alone.

Use superpowers:finishing-a-development-branch.

## Step 1: Verify Tests

Run the project's full test suite (`npm test` / `cargo test` / `pytest` / `go test ./...`).

**If tests fail**, report the failures and stop — the menu comes after a green suite:

```
Tests failing (<N> failures). Must fix before completing:

[Show failures]
```

**If tests pass:** continue to Step 2.

## Step 2: Detect Environment

```bash
GIT_DIR=$(cd "$(git rev-parse --git-dir)" 2>/dev/null && pwd -P)
GIT_COMMON=$(cd "$(git rev-parse --git-common-dir)" 2>/dev/null && pwd -P)
# Capture now, while still inside the workspace — Step 5 changes directory
# before cleanup (Step 6) needs this value
WORKTREE_PATH=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)
```

This determines which menu to show and how cleanup works:

| State | Menu | Cleanup |
|-------|------|---------|
| `GIT_DIR == GIT_COMMON` (normal repo) | Standard 3 options | No worktree to clean up |
| `GIT_DIR != GIT_COMMON`, named branch | Standard 3 options | Provenance-based (see Step 6) |
| `GIT_DIR != GIT_COMMON`, detached HEAD | Reduced 2 options (no merge) | Externally managed — leave in place |

## Step 3: Determine Base Branch

The base branch is whatever this work forked from — usually named in the
plan, the conversation, or the branch's upstream. If it is not already
known, ask: "This branch split from <your best guess> - is that correct?"
Confirm before merging: merging into the wrong base is expensive to undo.

## Step 4: Present Options

**Normal repo and named-branch worktree — present exactly these 3 options:**

```
Implementation complete. What would you like to do?

1. Merge back to <base-branch> locally
2. Push and create a Pull Request
3. Keep the branch as-is (I'll handle it later)

Which option?
```

**Detached HEAD — present exactly these 2 options:**

```
Implementation complete. You're on a detached HEAD (externally managed workspace).

1. Push as new branch and create a Pull Request
2. Keep as-is (I'll handle it later)

Which option?
```

Present the menu exactly as written — concise, with every option coming
from the list above. Discarding the work happens only in response to your
human partner explicitly asking for it (see "If your human partner asks to
discard the work" below). Wait for their answer; the integration decision
is theirs.

steps.title: Design before implementation
steps.description: Choose the feature route, explore the design and obtain approval.

steps.title: Plan and choose execution
steps.description: Review the task plan, then select subagents or native execution.

steps.title: Implement and review a task
steps.description: The subagent route separates implementation and task review.

steps.title: Bound the review loop
steps.description: Revisit findings within the round limit; record adjudicated or parked results.

steps.title: Record progress and continue
steps.description: Both execution methods record task completion and continue until branch review.

steps.title: Review the branch and decide
steps.description: Complete whole-branch review, then run the full suite before offering integration choices.

uncertainties: This is a static map of instructions, not an observed agent run or a guarantee that agents follow them.
Scope: feature development. Debugging and other entry routes are not expanded. Small changes and explicitly approved exceptions may bypass design planning.
Review outcomes can include deferred or parked issues; task completion does not mean that every issue was fixed. Branch integration remains a user choice.

cs.title: Superpowers: vývoj nové funkce
cs.question: Jak Superpowers vede novou funkci od návrhu k dokončení větve?
cs.summary: Předepsané workflow s volbou způsobu práce, kontrolou úloh, omezenými opravnými smyčkami a rozhodnutím o integraci.

router.label: Výběr relevantních skillů
router.description: Vstupní instrukce volí skilly podle úkolu. Graf sleduje návrh nové funkce; ladění a další postupy mají jiné vstupní body.

design.label: Prozkoumání a zápis návrhu
design.description: Vyjasní se záměr, cíle, omezení a přístupy a zapíše se návrh. Malé změny nebo výslovně domluvené výjimky mohou mít kratší cestu.

approval.label: Schválení návrhu
approval.description: Běžná cesta nové funkce vyžaduje schválení návrhu uživatelem před implementací a pokračuje do writing-plans. Jde o pravidlo v instrukcích, nikoli technicky vynucenou bránu.

plan.label: Zápis a kontrola plánu
plan.description: Vznikne plán s úlohami, zaškrtávacími kroky a ověřením. Vlastní kontrola posoudí pokrytí specifikace, konzistenci a testy.

choice.label: Volba způsobu provedení
choice.description: Zachová se dříve zvolený způsob; jinak uživatel vybere vývoj se subagenty nebo přímou práci v aktuálním agentovi. Obě cesty probíhají v témže sezení.

controller.label: Řízení subagentů
controller.description: Připraví pracovní prostor a záznam, pro každou úlohu vyšle nového implementera, zodpovídá otázky, koordinuje kontroly a vybírá další úlohy.

implementer.label: Implementace, testy a vlastní kontrola
implementer.description: Implementer řeší úlohu, testuje, commituje a sám ji kontroluje. Otázky se vracejí řídícímu agentovi k doplnění kontextu.

review.label: Kontrola jednotlivé úlohy
review.description: Dokončená úloha se kontroluje vůči specifikaci a kvalitě kódu. Schválení ji uzavře; nálezy přecházejí do omezené opravné smyčky.

fix.label: Omezená opravná smyčka
fix.description: Nejvýše pět kol oprav: v kolech 1–3 pokračuje původní implementer, v kolech 4–5 nastupuje nový a schopnější. Znovu se kontroluje dotčený rozsah; na limitu se nálezy rozhodnou, odloží nebo zaparkují podle pravidel.

inline.label: Přímé provedení plánu
inline.description: Aktuální agent provádí kroky plánu, používá TDD a ověřování, řeší neshody a před zápisem úlohy zkontroluje podmínky dokončení.

ledger.label: Záznam úloh a další úloha
ledger.description: Eviduje se plán, postup, testy a commity. Úloha se podle pravidel dokončí nebo zaparkuje; pak se pokračuje zbývajícími úlohami či kontrolou celé větve.

final.label: Kontrola celé větve
final.description: Zkontroluje se celá větev včetně odložených a zaparkovaných nálezů. Následuje nejvýše jedna vlna oprav a jedna cílená kontrola, rozhodnutí o zbytku a při čistém výsledku úklid pracovního prostoru.

finish.label: Testy a volba integrace
finish.description: Spustí se celá testovací sada; chyby zastaví nabídku integrace. Při úspěchu se nabídnou možnosti podle prostředí: sloučení, push/PR nebo ponechání větve. Rozhoduje uživatel.

design-path.title: Návrh před implementací
design-path.description: Vybere se cesta funkce, připraví návrh a získá schválení.

planning.title: Plán a volba provedení
planning.description: Zkontroluje se plán úloh a vyberou subagenti nebo přímé provedení.

task.title: Implementace a kontrola úlohy
task.description: Cesta subagentů odděluje implementaci a kontrolu úlohy.

fixing.title: Omezení opravné smyčky
fixing.description: Nálezy se řeší v omezeném počtu kol; rozhodnuté či zaparkované výsledky se zapíší.

iterate.title: Zápis postupu a pokračování
iterate.description: Oba způsoby zapisují dokončení úloh a pokračují ke kontrole větve.

integrate.title: Kontrola větve a rozhodnutí
integrate.description: Dokončí se kontrola celé větve a poté testy před nabídkou integrace.

uncertainties: Statická mapa instrukcí, nikoli pozorovaný běh agenta ani záruka jejich dodržení.
Rozsah: vývoj nové funkce. Ladění a další vstupní cesty nejsou rozvedené. Malé změny a výslovně schválené výjimky mohou návrh a plánování přeskočit.
Kontroly mohou skončit odloženými nebo zaparkovanými nálezy; dokončení úlohy neznamená opravu všech problémů. Integraci větve volí uživatel.

de.title: Superpowers: ein Feature entwickeln
de.question: Wie führt Superpowers vom Design zum Abschluss eines Branches?
de.summary: Vorgeschriebener Ablauf mit Ausführungswahl, Aufgabenprüfungen, begrenzten Korrekturen und Integrationsentscheidung.

router.label: Passende Skills wählen
router.description: Die Einstiegsanweisungen wählen Skills für die Aufgabe. Dieser Graph folgt dem Feature-Design; Debugging und andere Abläufe sind nicht ausgeführt.

design.label: Design erkunden und dokumentieren
design.description: Absicht, Ziele, Grenzen und Ansätze klären und dokumentieren. Kleine Änderungen oder ausdrücklich vereinbarte Ausnahmen können einen kürzeren Weg nehmen.

approval.label: Designfreigabe
approval.description: Der normale Feature-Ablauf verlangt vor der Umsetzung die Freigabe des Nutzers, danach writing-plans. Dies ist eine Anweisung, keine technisch erzwungene Sperre.

plan.label: Plan schreiben und prüfen
plan.description: Aufgaben, Checkbox-Schritte und Prüfungen festlegen. Die Selbstprüfung kontrolliert Spezifikationsabdeckung, Konsistenz und Tests.

choice.label: Ausführungsmethode wählen
choice.description: Eine bestehende Wahl bleibt erhalten; sonst wählt der Nutzer zwischen Subagenten und direkter Ausführung. Beide laufen in derselben Sitzung.

controller.label: Subagenten koordinieren
controller.description: Arbeitsbereich und Protokoll vorbereiten, je Aufgabe einen neuen Implementierer beauftragen, Fragen beantworten, Reviews koordinieren und weitere Aufgaben wählen.

implementer.label: Implementieren, testen und selbst prüfen
implementer.description: Der Implementierer bearbeitet, testet, committet und prüft die Aufgabe. Rückfragen gehen für zusätzlichen Kontext an den Controller.

review.label: Aufgabe prüfen
review.description: Spezifikationskonformität und Codequalität prüfen. Freigabe schließt die Aufgabe ab; Befunde gehen in die begrenzte Korrekturschleife.

fix.label: Begrenzte Korrekturschleife
fix.description: Höchstens fünf Runden: 1–3 mit dem ursprünglichen Implementierer, 4–5 mit neuer, leistungsfähigerer Hilfe. Betroffenen Umfang erneut prüfen; am Limit entscheiden, verschieben oder parken.

inline.label: Direkte Ausführung
inline.description: Der aktuelle Agent arbeitet den Plan mit TDD und Prüfungen ab, behandelt Abweichungen und kontrolliert die Abschlussbedingungen vor dem Protokollieren.

ledger.label: Aufgabenprotokoll und Fortsetzung
ledger.description: Plan, Fortschritt, Tests und Commits erfassen. Aufgaben regelgemäß abschließen oder parken, dann weitere Aufgaben oder den ganzen Branch prüfen.

final.label: Gesamten Branch prüfen
final.description: Auch verschobene und geparkte Befunde prüfen. Eine Korrekturwelle und eine gezielte Nachprüfung zulassen, verbleibende Befunde entscheiden und bei sauberem Review den Arbeitsbereich aufräumen.

finish.label: Tests und Integration wählen
finish.description: Die gesamte Testsuite ausführen. Fehler stoppen das Integrationsmenü. Bei Erfolg umgebungsabhängig Merge, Push/PR oder Beibehalten anbieten. Der Nutzer entscheidet.

design-path.title: Design vor Umsetzung
design-path.description: Feature-Route wählen, Design erkunden und Freigabe einholen.

planning.title: Planen und Methode wählen
planning.description: Aufgabenplan prüfen, dann Subagenten oder direkte Ausführung wählen.

task.title: Aufgabe implementieren und prüfen
task.description: Die Subagenten-Route trennt Implementierung und Aufgabenprüfung.

fixing.title: Review-Schleife begrenzen
fixing.description: Befunde innerhalb des Rundenlimits bearbeiten und Entscheidungen oder geparkte Ergebnisse erfassen.

iterate.title: Fortschritt erfassen
iterate.description: Beide Methoden protokollieren Aufgaben und gehen bis zum Branch-Review weiter.

integrate.title: Branch prüfen und entscheiden
integrate.description: Branch-Review abschließen und die gesamte Suite vor Integrationsoptionen ausführen.

uncertainties: Statische Karte von Anweisungen, kein beobachteter Agentenlauf und keine Garantie ihrer Befolgung.
Umfang: Feature-Entwicklung. Debugging und andere Einstiege sind nicht ausgeführt. Kleine Änderungen und genehmigte Ausnahmen können Design und Planung überspringen.
Reviews können verschobene oder geparkte Befunde hinterlassen. Aufgabenabschluss bedeutet nicht, dass jedes Problem behoben wurde. Integration bleibt eine Nutzerentscheidung.

fr.title: Superpowers : développer une fonctionnalité
fr.question: Comment Superpowers guide-t-il de la conception à la fin d’une branche ?
fr.summary: Un processus prescrit avec choix d’exécution, revues des tâches, corrections limitées et décision d’intégration.

router.label: Choisir les skills adaptés
router.description: Les instructions d’entrée sélectionnent les skills. Ce graphe suit la conception d’une fonctionnalité ; les autres parcours ne sont pas développés.

design.label: Explorer et documenter la conception
design.description: Clarifier intention, objectifs, contraintes et approches, puis les écrire. Les petits changements et exceptions explicites peuvent suivre un chemin plus court.

approval.label: Approbation de la conception
approval.description: Le parcours normal demande l’accord de l’utilisateur avant de construire, puis passe à writing-plans. C’est une consigne, pas un verrou technique.

plan.label: Rédiger et vérifier le plan
plan.description: Définir tâches, étapes à cocher et vérifications. La revue personnelle contrôle couverture de la spécification, cohérence et tests.

choice.label: Choisir l’exécution
choice.description: Conserver un choix existant ; sinon l’utilisateur choisit sous-agents ou exécution directe. Les deux ont lieu dans la même session.

controller.label: Coordonner les sous-agents
controller.description: Préparer espace et registre, déléguer chaque tâche à un nouvel implémenteur, répondre aux questions et coordonner les revues et tâches suivantes.

implementer.label: Implémenter, tester et se relire
implementer.description: L’implémenteur réalise la tâche, teste, committe et se relit. Les questions reviennent au contrôleur pour préciser le contexte.

review.label: Revue de la tâche
review.description: Vérifier conformité et qualité du code. L’approbation termine la tâche ; les constats passent à la boucle de correction limitée.

fix.label: Corrections limitées
fix.description: Au plus cinq tours : implémenteur initial aux tours 1–3, aide nouvelle et plus capable aux tours 4–5. Revoir le périmètre affecté ; à la limite, arbitrer, différer ou mettre en attente.

inline.label: Exécution directe
inline.description: L’agent courant suit le plan avec TDD et vérifications, traite les écarts et vérifie le contrat de fin avant d’enregistrer chaque tâche.

ledger.label: Registre et tâche suivante
ledger.description: Consigner plan, progression, tests et commits. Terminer ou mettre en attente selon les règles, puis continuer ou revoir toute la branche.

final.label: Revue de toute la branche
final.description: Inclure les constats différés et en attente. Une vague de corrections et une revue ciblée, puis arbitrage du reste et nettoyage si la revue est propre.

finish.label: Tests et choix d’intégration
finish.description: Exécuter toute la suite. Les échecs bloquent le menu d’intégration. Si elle réussit, proposer fusion, push/PR ou conservation selon l’environnement. L’utilisateur choisit.

e14.label: arbitré / mis en attente à la limite

e19.label: une vague de corrections et revue

design-path.title: Concevoir avant de construire
design-path.description: Choisir le parcours, explorer la conception et obtenir l’accord.

planning.title: Planifier et choisir
planning.description: Vérifier le plan puis choisir sous-agents ou exécution directe.

task.title: Implémenter et revoir une tâche
task.description: Le parcours délégué sépare implémentation et revue.

fixing.title: Limiter les corrections
fixing.description: Traiter les constats dans la limite prévue et consigner arbitrages ou mises en attente.

iterate.title: Consigner et continuer
iterate.description: Les deux méthodes enregistrent les tâches puis arrivent à la revue de branche.

integrate.title: Revoir la branche et décider
integrate.description: Terminer la revue puis exécuter toute la suite avant les options d’intégration.

uncertainties: Carte statique des consignes, pas une exécution observée ni une garantie de leur respect.
Périmètre : développement de fonctionnalités. Débogage et autres entrées non développés. Petites modifications et exceptions approuvées peuvent éviter conception et planification.
Des constats peuvent rester différés ou en attente. Finir une tâche ne signifie pas avoir tout corrigé. L’intégration reste un choix utilisateur.

es.title: Superpowers: desarrollar una función
es.question: ¿Cómo guía Superpowers desde el diseño hasta terminar la rama?
es.summary: Un flujo prescrito con opciones de ejecución, revisiones por tarea, correcciones limitadas y decisiones de integración.

router.label: Elegir skills relevantes
router.description: Las instrucciones iniciales seleccionan skills para la tarea. Este grafo sigue el diseño de funciones; depuración y otras rutas no se desarrollan.

design.label: Explorar y documentar el diseño
design.description: Aclarar intención, objetivos, restricciones y enfoques, y escribir el diseño. Cambios pequeños o excepciones acordadas pueden usar una ruta más corta.

approval.label: Aprobar el diseño
approval.description: La ruta normal exige aprobación del usuario antes de implementar y luego pasa a writing-plans. Es una instrucción, no un bloqueo técnico.

plan.label: Escribir y revisar el plan
plan.description: Definir tareas, pasos verificables y comprobaciones. La autorrevisión comprueba cobertura de la especificación, coherencia y pruebas.

choice.label: Elegir la ejecución
choice.description: Conservar una elección previa; si no existe, el usuario elige subagentes o ejecución directa. Ambas transcurren en la misma sesión.

controller.label: Coordinar subagentes
controller.description: Preparar espacio y registro, enviar cada tarea a un implementador nuevo, responder preguntas y coordinar revisiones y tareas siguientes.

implementer.label: Implementar, probar y autorrevisar
implementer.description: El implementador realiza la tarea, prueba, crea commits y revisa. Las preguntas vuelven al controlador para obtener contexto.

review.label: Revisar la tarea
review.description: Comprobar especificación y calidad. La aprobación termina la tarea; los hallazgos pasan al ciclo de corrección limitado.

fix.label: Ciclo de corrección limitado
fix.description: Hasta cinco rondas: implementador original en 1–3, ayuda nueva y más capaz en 4–5. Revisar el alcance afectado; al límite, resolver, aplazar o dejar pendiente según las reglas.

inline.label: Ejecución directa
inline.description: El agente actual sigue los pasos con TDD y verificaciones, trata discrepancias y comprueba el contrato de finalización antes de registrar cada tarea.

ledger.label: Registro y siguiente tarea
ledger.description: Anotar plan, progreso, pruebas y commits. Finalizar o dejar pendiente según las reglas y continuar tareas o revisar toda la rama.

final.label: Revisión de toda la rama
final.description: Incluir hallazgos aplazados y pendientes. Una ronda de correcciones y una revisión focalizada, resolver lo restante y limpiar el espacio cuando la revisión esté limpia.

finish.label: Pruebas y opción de integración
finish.description: Ejecutar toda la suite. Los fallos detienen el menú de integración. Si pasa, ofrecer fusión, push/PR o conservar según el entorno. Decide el usuario.

e19.label: una ronda de corrección y revisión

design-path.title: Diseñar antes de implementar
design-path.description: Elegir la ruta, explorar el diseño y obtener aprobación.

planning.title: Planificar y elegir
planning.description: Revisar el plan y elegir subagentes o ejecución directa.

task.title: Implementar y revisar una tarea
task.description: La ruta con subagentes separa implementación y revisión.

fixing.title: Limitar las correcciones
fixing.description: Tratar hallazgos dentro del límite y registrar resoluciones o pendientes.

iterate.title: Registrar y continuar
iterate.description: Ambos métodos registran tareas y continúan hasta revisar la rama.

integrate.title: Revisar la rama y decidir
integrate.description: Completar la revisión y ejecutar toda la suite antes de las opciones de integración.

uncertainties: Mapa estático de instrucciones, no una ejecución observada ni garantía de cumplimiento.
Alcance: desarrollo de funciones. Depuración y otras entradas no se desarrollan. Cambios pequeños y excepciones aprobadas pueden omitir diseño y planificación.
Las revisiones pueden dejar hallazgos aplazados o pendientes. Terminar una tarea no implica haber corregido todo. La integración sigue siendo decisión del usuario.

grounding.scope: Source existence, line ranges and fingerprints. The author must verify the interpretation; this is not a runtime trace.
